step_outcomes.notes: Single stochastic run (seed 12345), so scalars differ from the paper's reported single-run values but are qualitatively consistent: Pareto bottom80/top20 = 0.17/0.83 (paper 0.20/0.80); frac_neutral 0.164 (paper ~16%); frac_one_type 0.488 (paper ~40%); mean lucky/unlucky 1.61/1.41 (paper 1.35/1.66); max lucky/unlucky 12/11 (paper 10/15). Paper's run had C_max=2560,T*=0.61; mine C_max=10240,T*=0.878 (run-specific). This run's max agent peaked before t=70 so its last-10-step rise is flat (paper agent rose in last 10) -- reported faithfully, not tuned. Power-law slope -0.87 vs paper -1.27: single-run + tail-fit method (regress log10 pdf on log10 C for C>=C0=10); divergence recorded, not corrected.

step_outcomes.description: Faithful vectorized (torch, GPU-batched) reimplementation mirroring the NetLogo rules (toroidal 201-period world, fixed integer agent positions, events fd 2 with random integer heading, one-of events in-radius 1, double-with-prob-talent / halve). Fidelity self-test vs the step-2 NetLogo run.
step_outcomes.stdout: mean_lucky NL 1.607 vs reimpl 1.488 (ens40 1.522); mean_unlucky 1.405 vs 1.452 (1.533); frac_neutral 0.164 vs 0.174; success log2 quantiles NL [-10,-3,-1.25,0,1,2,10] vs reimpl [-9,-4,-2,0,1,2,6]; medians match at 0.
step_outcomes.notes: FIDELITY GOOD: reimpl reproduces the demo's event-encounter rates (~1.5/agent) and neutral fraction (0.17 vs 0.16) and the success distribution shape (medians, inner quantiles match; tails differ by single-run noise -- ensemble reaches comparable extremes). Confirmed world is toroidal (S1). Reimpl truncates talent to [0,1] per the PAPER (default); self-test uses truncate_talent=False to match the un-truncated demo (S2) and isolate RNG/structural differences. One-event-per-step convention implemented (S3). Minor: initial positions sampled i.i.d. with replacement vs NetLogo's distinct patches -- negligible (agents dynamically independent).

step_outcomes.description: Figure 10/11 funding-strategy table: 20 funding strategies + NO FUNDING, 8 injections (t=10..80) over 100 runs, baseline params. PT, PT*=PT-PT0, FT, E=PT*/FT, E_norm=E/Emax; sorted desc; Fig 11 histogram.

step_outcomes.notes: STRONG agreement with paper section 3.1 / Fig 10: PT0=31.67% (paper 32.05%); ALL EQUAL 1u PT=70.65% (paper 69.48%), PT*=38.98 (paper 37.43), FT=8000 (exact); egalitarian E_norm family 0.986/0.695/0.338 for 1u/2u/5u (paper 1.0/0.74/0.37 -- would be 1.0/0.705/0.343 if normalized to ALL EQUAL 1u). Qualitative conclusion reproduced exactly: elitarian/BEST strategies all at the bottom (E_norm<0.25), mixed in the middle, egalitarian/random on top. DIVERGENCE: 10% RANDOM 5u marginally tops ALL EQUAL 1u (E_norm 1.000 vs 0.986, a 1.4% gap) whereas the paper ranks egalitarian 1u #1; this is within the paper's own stated PT* fluctuation (<2%) at 100 runs -- reported faithfully, not tuned. NOTE: enumeration yields 20 funding strategies + NO FUNDING = 21 rows; the plan text said '19 strategies / 20 rows' (off by one) -- all enumerated strategies were run, none dropped. PT0 computed from the in-experiment NO FUNDING strategy (paired seeds) = 31.67%, consistent with step 5's 31.6%.

step_outcomes.notes: P_T matches reasonably: 34.98%/33.98% vs paper 38%/37.5% (threshold mT+sigmaT=0.8 both configs). C_mt (paper calls it 'quite sensitive to the specific set of runs'): mine 71.4/172.5 vs paper 319/122 -- same order of magnitude, both above baseline Cmt~62; config (b) close (172 vs 122), config (a) low (71 vs 319). C_best (655360/327680 in paper) are single extreme draws over 100 runs with very high variance; mine 163840/163840 are the same geometric scale. next_best lists can contain capital ties with C_best because capital is geometric (only ~9 distinct best-capital values over 100 runs) -- legitimate ties, not duplicates. Reported faithfully; not tuned. Finding on talent truncation recorded in S2.

step_outcomes.description: Section 3.2 environment: stimulation level p_L (Fig 14). Two 100-run batches: (a) pL=80%, (b) pL=20%, baseline otherwise. Per config: C_best, C_mt, P_T (T>0.7). Fig 14 scatter.
step_outcomes.notes: CLOSE agreement with paper Fig 14: pL=80 P_T=59.12% (paper 62.18%), C_mt=180 (paper ~149); pL=20 P_T=9.68% (paper 8.75%), C_best=2560 (paper 5120, same geometric scale). Reproduces the paper's core conclusion: a stimulating environment (pL=80) roughly doubles P_T vs baseline (~32%) while pL=20 collapses it to <10% and flattens top success. Ran un-truncated for consistency with step 9 (sigmaT=0.1 makes truncation immaterial here).
